Action Plan:
1) Attend an in-person clinic/GP surgery for assessment of wheeze and shortness of breath; evaluation to include finger pulse oximetry (oxygen saturation) to help distinguish asthma exacerbation vs allergic reaction.
2) If available prior to attending, take an oral antihistamine (for possible dust-related allergy). If none at home, obtain an over-the-counter antihistamine on the way; if unable, the clinic/GP can prescribe.
3) Systemic steroids may be required depending on in-person assessment and test results; decision deferred to examining clinician.
4) A summary letter of this consult will be sent via the app for the patient to take to the GP/clinic.
5) Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Reason for visit: Wheezing and shortness of breath.
- History of presenting complaint:
  - Onset: Began approximately 2 days ago, about 1 hour after cleaning house with significant dust exposure.
  - Duration/progression: Persistent for 2 days; worse at night.
  - Severity/impact: Feels short of breath; sometimes unable to complete sentences when talking.
  - Associated symptoms: Denies chest pain with deep breaths. Denies dizziness.
  - Hydration: Drinking ~4–5 glasses of water/day.
  - Treatments tried: None taken for the wheeze.
- Past medical history:
  - Childhood asthma; occasionally symptomatic with prolonged running.
  - Seasonal hay fever (summer).
- Previous treatments:
  - Has an asthma inhaler at home (type not documented; “from a couple of months ago”); not currently used for this episode. Dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Has taken steroids for asthma in the past; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Medications: No regular hay fever medications. Otherwise not documented.
- Allergies: No known allergies reported.
- Social/Environmental: Recent heavy dust exposure while cleaning. Proximity to GP/clinic: a short drive (exact time not specified).

Objective:
- No in-person examination or vital signs obtained during this teleconsult; video connection was lost partway through the call.
- No investigations performed during this consult.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Acute wheeze and shortness of breath after dust exposure
   - Assessment or likely diagnosis: Suspected asthma exacerbation vs allergic reaction to dust exposure.
   - Differential diagnosis: Asthma exacerbation; allergic reaction.
   - Investigations planned: In-person assessment with pulse oximetry (oxygen saturation).
   - Treatment planned: Take an oral antihistamine prior to attending if available; otherwise obtain OTC en route or have clinic/GP prescribe. Systemic steroids may be required pending in-person findings.
   - Relevant referrals: In-person evaluation at clinic/GP. Summary letter sent via app for GP/clinic.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals (including respiratory rate, heart rate, oxygen saturation), peak flow/spirometry, physical exam findings, comprehensive medication list and doses, smoking status, full allergy details (drug/food/environmental), safety-net/emergency advice, explicit timeframe for in-person review.
- Internal conflicts: Location for in-person review alternately described as “one of our clinics” and “the GP surgery” (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Some audio dropouts and lost video; several incomplete statements; no quantitative clinical data captured.
